newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary coupons plunge for lack of buying choice.
newsitem.headline: Hungary coupons plunge for lack of buying choice.

text.p: A three-day tumble in the prices of compensation coupons on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday resulted from a lack of any near-term opportunities to use the papers, traders said.
The fall accelerated on Thursday when coupons opened at 730 forints, below Wednesday's close of 815 forints, and at 1146 GMT they stood at 681 forints.
The papers reached a 52-week high of 931 forints on Monday but have since gradually declined to close at 900 forints on Tuesday and at 815 forints on Wednesday.

"Subscriptions in (electricity supplier) Elmu Rt are over, so we are again where we were recently, namely that investors don't have any opportunities to use their coupons, at least for the time being," one trader said.
Compensation coupons were awarded to victims of expropriation under Hungary's former fascist and communist regimes.
The coupons can be used as payment in the country's privatisation process.
